creator: Alexander Terp
description:
There is no config layer at all today. `DaemonId("local")` is a constant (crates/muster-seam/src/session.rs) already commented as a placeholder for configuration, and `Keymap::default()` is a hardcoded table. The README's 'Configuration is files' is aspirational.

The remote arc forces the daemon half: naming a second daemon is exactly what a config file is for, and `Endpoint` has been a one-variant enum waiting for it since composition landed.

Split so the core stays honest about I/O: parsing is pure and lives in muster-core (text in, a Config out), conformance-tested like every other decidable thing; reading the file happens at the edge, in the seam's Startup handler, from a path the shell chooses - the same division `discover_socket_path` already uses by taking an environment map rather than reading one.

The keymap half is a different card (a_26BJGXAS9) and should not be pulled in here: `Action` in the core keymap is an empty enum, so binding chords is real work rather than a second table.

A missing or unparseable config is not fatal. It falls back to discovering the local daemon from the environment, and says so in a line that names what was lost.
title: ⚙️ Config is a file, and the daemon list is its first citizen
